scope: Individual A7 and common README proof/contract audit against D1/D5/R0 and declared Foster/path semantics. No implementation, physical qualification or whole-interface composition acceptance.

findings.reason: The successor containment argument is the D1 induction with a joint input/state relation. Rounded/compressed representation must contain the reach/measurement intersection. A probabilistic lifetime claim requires a joint event, not repeated independent nominal confidence declarations.

Reference R increases and Q/C decreases remain user-proposed physical hypotheses. Positive tau=R*C has no forced direction. Reversible thermal response is separated, and neither manufacturing spread nor an engineering envelope supplies an aging rate.

findings.location: Conditional containment theorem, sentence beginning It cannot justify narrow uncertainty
findings.reason: The unconditional narrowness statement is stronger than reviewed D5. Monotonicity plus a narrow remaining physical support can retain useful narrowness without a rate or new measurement. The preceding statement about traversing the remaining support is correct; the inference as written omits the essential support-width qualification.
findings.counterexample: For monotone increase with support [0,1] and known p(0)=1-epsilon, every future p lies in [1-epsilon,1], arbitrarily narrow as epsilon tends to zero. At p(0)=1 it is a singleton.
findings.required_change: State that monotonicity alone cannot justify an endpoint tighter than the remaining qualified support, or useful narrowness when that remaining support is too wide; retain the near-endpoint exception from D5.

findings.location: Historical evidence and state consistency, varying-capacity SOC sum
findings.reason: The stated sum is valid under the inherited SOC-continuous capacity convention and exact/qualified input integration. Piecewise-constant effective capacity alone does not specify SOC transport at a capacity change. A7 permits a general evolution relation but presents this particular SOC law unconditionally; R0 proves only stationary Q and the older L6 explicitly names SOC continuity.
findings.counterexample: At zero current let Q change from 0.06 Ah to 0.05 Ah at z=0.4. A law preserving remaining charge Q*z gives z_next=0.48, whereas the displayed sum with no capacity-jump correction gives 0.4. Both remain inside ordinary SOC support; choosing the physical law is an open premise, not an arithmetic decision.
findings.required_change: Explicitly condition the displayed sum on dz/dt=-I/(3600Q(t)) with SOC continuous at capacity changes and the qualified current/interval convention. State that an alternative physical loss/charge/SOC transport law needs its additional terms/maps and qualification. Preserve the path-dependence warning under the chosen law.

findings.reason: Under the SOC-continuous law, capacity paths with the same final Q and signed charge can give different SOC. Continuous-time form is z_N=z_0-integral I(t)/(3600Q(t)) dt. A current health centroid cannot replace the joint path without a separate bounded argument.
findings.witness: In arbitrary consistent charge/capacity units, three equal charge increments 0.1 with monotone Q paths (2,2,1) and (2,1,1) have common initial/final Q and total charge, but SOC decrements 0.20 and 0.25. This is an algebraic witness, not a calibrated aging rate.

findings.reason: Pole crossings demand a joint relabeling/domain policy, not scalar sorting. Under a permutation all branch R,C,tau,v coordinates and their uncertainty/history must move together to preserve summed voltage and future response. Voltage continuity versus C*v continuity is correctly left as an unresolved physical relation.

Unknown I/T/clock, thermal coefficients, hysteresis, sensor-offset drift and correlations remain in the joint evolution/input contract. Set and density semantics are distinct; probabilistic normalizers, support masses and Jacobians are retained, with once-only evidence. No stationary R0 coefficient map is claimed for an unqualified time-varying model.

Physical calibration, useful reacquisition, aging reset support, state-map controls and false-authorization/availability tests remain acceptance obligations. The contract selects no process noise, drift rate, forgetting factor, knot count or deployable aging law.

validation.method: Premise-by-premise handwritten proof audit and algebraic counterexamples against D1/D5/R0 and earlier physical-path qualifications. No simulations or implementation tests needed for this contract-only review.
validation.artifact_policy: Exclusive creation of this receipt only; no proof, implementation or existing result edited.

remaining_application_obligations: Qualify the admitted battery/population/use/temperature family and actual joint initial/evolution/measurement uncertainty.
Select and qualify SOC/capacity and RC voltage/charge transport, including capacity loss, pole crossings and relabeling of full joint state.
Bind quantitative aging/thermal/input restrictions if useful quiet-period uncertainty requires them; do not infer rates from a prior range or smoothness.
Prove approximation/rounding reach inclusions or probability-law fidelity and a valid simultaneous risk event.
Instantiate aged-cell resets, informative reacquisition scenarios/deadlines, sensor drift and thermal-cycle tests.
Complete separate continuous-shape representation, query, lifetime availability and full M23 resource obligations.
remaining_limits: Decision is bound to exact listed A7/common README hashes. Required substantive revisions need a renewed independent review.
This is a conditional mathematical/contract review, not physical coverage or a deployable aging-model certificate.
No whole-architecture interfaces.json/requirements.json composition acceptance is included.
